description:
fz-5xp.17 aligned Json to Elixir's API for the functions fz can express. Three
parts of lib/elixir/lib/json.ex are not followed yet, each needing something fz
does not have:

  * encode_to_iodata!/1,2 -- returns IODATA, a nested list of binaries written
    without being flattened first. fz has no iodata concept, and adding one is a
    decision about the value model rather than about JSON.

  * protocol_encode/2 and the JSON.Encoder PROTOCOL. Elixir's is derivable, so a
    struct opts in and names its encodable fields with :only or :except. fz has
    protocols but no derivation, and those options are what make the protocol
    safe to use on structs at all -- Elixir's own docs warn about leaking
    private fields when neither is given.

  * decode/3, which takes an accumulator and a keyword list of decoders
    (array_start, array_push, array_finish, object_start, ...) so a caller can
    build something other than lists and maps without a second pass. fz has
    Keyword now, so the shape is expressible; what it needs is the decision
    about whether the decoder is written to be customisable that way.

The first two are the interesting ones: both are about fz's protocol story
rather than about JSON, and the Encoder protocol overlaps fz-5xp.70
(Collectable) in asking what a derivable protocol looks like here.
title: Json: the rest of Elixir's JSON surface -- Encoder protocol, iodata, custom decoders
